name: Magnet CTF 2020 Windows — Piracy Ecosystem and Insecure Configuration
description: Windows 7 x64 VMware VM (ComputerName: WIN-9H6J4FBP8F7, Volume: TestOS, IP: 192.168.10.146) belonging to user Warren. Registry analysis reveals a coordinated piracy toolkit installation: KMSAuto scheduled task for persistent Windows/Office activation bypass, trashreg.exe registry cleaner from NSIS temp directory, and Office Tab Enterprise — all installed within a 155-second window on 2020-02-14. The system runs RDP with NLA disabled on an EOL Windows 7 OS, creating a Sticky Keys exploitation vector. No C2 patterns or external compromise indicators detected in memory analysis. Gambling software (Ignition Casino Poker) installed on what appears to be a corporate-provisioned VM with Office 2013 Professional Plus and multilingual MUI packs (Ukrainian, Russian, English, French, Spanish, German).

artifacts.description: KMSAuto scheduled task registered at \KMSAuto (root-level, outside \Microsoft\ hierarchy). Task Reg Time: 2020-02-14 19:42:21Z. Task Last Run: 2020-04-20 01:12:47Z. KMSAuto is a well-documented Windows/Office activation bypass tool that emulates a Key Management Service. Persistence via scheduled task ensures re-activation across reboots. 67-day gap between registration and last run confirms ongoing operation.

peirce_expected.firstness: Three registry artifacts within 155 seconds: KMSAuto task (19:42:21Z), trashreg.exe AppPaths from NSIS temp (19:42:33Z), Office Tab Enterprise uninstall (19:44:56Z). Empty Licenses key. RDP enabled with NLA disabled. Memory shows legitimate processes and no C2.
peirce_expected.secondness: KMSAuto is structurally inconsistent with legitimate activation (should use osppsvc/SoftwareProtectionPlatform). Root-level scheduled task placement is non-standard. NSIS temp directory is canonical piracy installer pattern. 12-second and 155-second temporal gaps indicate automated sequential installation. Empty Licenses key confirms activation bypass. RDP without NLA on EOL OS creates exploitation vector but no exploitation evidence exists.
peirce_expected.thirdness: Deliberate software license evasion through coordinated piracy toolkit. The actor made sequential decisions to install, persist, and maintain a piracy ecosystem over 67 days and 24 logins. The absence of concealment (plainly named KMSAuto, visible AppPaths, standard Uninstall entry) distinguishes INTENT from MALICE. Insecure RDP is convenience-driven negligence, not deliberate attack preparation.

devil_advocate: This is a CTF lab VM (Volume: TestOS, auto-generated hostname WIN-9H6J4FBP8F7). The piracy toolkit may have been pre-installed by the CTF organizer to create the forensic challenge scenario. In a lab/CTF context, piracy may be irrelevant to the investigation. RDP with NLA disabled is standard practice for VMware lab VMs. However, the artifacts themselves demonstrate genuine deliberate license evasion regardless of who performed it — the decisions required (install, persist, allow re-execution) cannot be explained by accident.
_label_correction_20260713: INTENT does not exist in the motor verdict scale (5 values: MALICE/SUSPICION/UNKNOWN/NOISE/ABSTAIN). Relabeled to SUSPICION — legacy pre-motor vocabulary. No active concealment layer (KMSAuto task evasion is licensing bypass, not anti-forensics against an investigator).
notes: Primary finding is deliberate software piracy (KMSAuto + trashreg + Office Tab Enterprise) — INTENT without concealment. Secondary: insecure RDP (SUSPICION). No external compromise detected. Memory analysis confirms all legitimate processes and network connections. NTUSER.DAT and Prefetch not available — UserAssist, shellbags, and execution counts are unknown limitations.
